given_word.instructions: Pick the clearest short Given declaration word for a reusable locally described modifier attached to models/fields, including schema/defaults/pure constraints and explicitly declared supporting hooks.

criteria.trait: trait completable "description": a reusable local modifier on a declaration. It is concise and specific to attachment/composition; documentation must avoid implying inheritance or a full trait/interface-conformance system.
criteria.feature: feature completable "description": a reusable local feature applied to selected declarations. It is accessible and broad enough for supporting hooks, but may sound app-level rather than a model/field modifier.
criteria.behavior: behavior completable "description": a locally described reusable behavior applied to selected declarations. It conveys custom execution as well as rules, but may imply effects for field/default-only features.
criteria.open: Leave naming open if the desired extension target/composition contract needs more clarification; the architecture and runtime target need not be rejected.

when_carrier.instructions: Choose the least intrusive way to express a generated implementation within an existing typed/authorized When scenario.

criteria.do_prompt: Keep scenario name/signature/by and add do "description" as an alternative to the ordinary indented do body. The quoted header clearly selects new generation syntax and avoids another word; its build-time meaning needs documentation.
criteria.do_generate: Keep scenario name/signature/by and add do generate "description" as the prompted-body alternative. An explicit generation word makes phase intent visible and can be reused by view generation, at the cost of repeated syntax.
criteria.implement: Keep scenario name/signature/by and use implement "description" as the prompted-body alternative to do. It clearly describes supplying implementation and is short, but introduces a new scenario child keyword.
criteria.open: Keep the exact carrier spelling undecided until the generated-JS interface/effects contract is concrete; do not block the category map.
